chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: “The apostate is separated from his wife, his slaughtered animal is not to be eaten, and he is asked to repent for three days. If he repents, otherwise he is killed on the fourth day.”

key_terms.الْمُرْتَدُّ: the apostate; one who has turned back from Islam
key_terms.تَابَ: he repented; he returned from apostasy
key_terms.تُعْزَلُ: is separated; here, his wife is separated from him
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: three days; the period granted for repentance
key_terms.ذَبِيحَتُهُ: his slaughtered animal; meat slaughtered by him
key_terms.قُتِلَ: he was killed; the legal punishment mentioned in the report
key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: he is asked to repent; he is given an opportunity to return

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the apostate in Tahdhib al-Ahkam according to Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the apostate in Shia fiqh. It mentions the separation of his wife from him, the prohibition of eating his slaughtered animal, and a three-day period in which he is called to repentance before punishment is carried out if he does not repent.
